name: glucose_limitation_yield
title: Glucose-limitation yield response
claim: Final dynamic-FBA biomass scales with the initial glucose supply: a glucose-limited cell (2 mM) reaches roughly a quarter of the biomass of a glucose-replete cell (10 mM), the quantitative carbon-limitation response.

purpose.question: Does the biomass yield of dynamic-FBA growth scale with the initial glucose supply — the quantitative signature of carbon limitation?
purpose.mechanism: New biology-forward study (discovery engine): a new configuration/analysis of a real spatio-flux composite.
purpose.expected_outcome: The quantitative behavior tests pass, confirming the stated emergent/metabolic claim.

question: Does the biomass yield of dynamic-FBA growth scale with the initial glucose supply — the quantitative signature of carbon limitation?

behavior_tests.name: GLUCOSE-LIMITATION-LOW-YIELD
behavior_tests.description: glucose-limited (2 mM) final biomass lands in the low-yield band.

behavior_tests.name: GLUCOSE-LIMITATION-HIGH-YIELD
behavior_tests.description: glucose-replete (10 mM) final biomass lands in the high-yield band.

findings.statement: Biomass yield tracks the carbon supply: 2 mM glucose yields ~0.26 biomass vs ~0.96 at 10 mM — a ~4x yield difference set by the initial glucose, the quantitative carbon-limitation response (a real biological claim, not an artifact check).

resolved: Dynamic-FBA biomass yield scales with initial glucose.
remaining: Whether the yield-vs-glucose relationship is linear or saturating across a wider range is unmeasured.

followup_study_proposals.motivation: Two points show scaling; a glucose dose-response sweep would map whether yield is linear or saturating in the carbon supply.

falsifiability: If final biomass were independent of the initial glucose (the same yield at 2 and 10 mM), the carbon-limitation claim would be false.
limitations: Two glucose levels (not a full dose-response); a single genome-scale core model.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The yield gap is a transient that would close with more time.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: Both runs reach a biomass plateau as glucose is exhausted, so the gap is a yield limit, not a transient.
